speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah
text: asked the Minister for Home Affairs (a) in the past year, how many people have been penalised for jaywalking; (b) how does the Ministry monitor areas where jaywalking is prevalent; (c) how many fatal traffic accidents were caused by jaywalking in the past three years; (d) whether the Ministry plans to implement additional measures to reduce the danger of fatal traffic accidents to the elderly who jaywalk; and (e) whether there is a need to review the current penalties to deter jaywalking.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: In recent years, TP have stepped up its engagement of elderly pedestrians.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: In 2019, TP organised the Road Safety Carnival themed "Be Seen, Be Safe" for more than 1,000 senior citizens, to raise awareness on the importance of using designated pedestrian crossings and how to cross roads safely.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: This year, TP will be working with the Lion Befrienders Service Association and the National Trades Union Congress (NTUC) Health Co-operative Limited to train staff and volunteers to become Road Safety Champions to engage senior citizens on road safety.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: To further improve safety for elderly pedestrians, the Land Transport Authority (LTA) has implemented Silver Zones at locations with a high proportion of senior residents, and where there have been accidents involving seniors.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: Silver Zones have senior-friendly road safety features, such as rest points for pedestrians along road dividers and signs to alert motorists of the presence of elderly pedestrians.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: TP regularly conducts enforcement operations at accident-prone locations and jaywalking hotspots.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: Under the Road Traffic Act, it is an offence for pedestrians to fail to cross at a pedestrian crossing.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: We will monitor the situation and consider further measures if necessary.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: I do not have five supplementary questions, but I have two.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: When I first came to Singapore, many of my cousins told me, "Don't jaywalk.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: You have to cross by following traffic rules.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: Otherwise, the Police will catch you and will fine you." Therefore, I am very law-abiding.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: But today, I cannot say the same thing to the visitors to Singapore because you can see jaywalkers everywhere.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: To many of us, we feel that there is no enforcement or very little enforcement.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary mentioned just now 59 fatal accidents involving jaywalkers.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: The second question is, I also have residents who give feedback that increasingly, that when pedestrians cross the roads, their eyes are glued to the phone.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: Currently, we know that this is not enforceable.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: As I had mentioned in my earlier reply, definitely, more education, more outreach will be conducted by TP.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: I have spoken about the "Be Seen, Be Safe" campaign.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: We will also be working with more community outreach organisations, such as Lion Befrienders and NTUC Health Co-operative.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: The Member mentioned that, anecdotally, what she sees on the roads is that there are more and more jaywalkers.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: We are aligned in wanting to deter pedestrians from jaywalking because it definitely causes a danger to themselves.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: So, we have to find effective ways of reaching out to them to tell them that this is dangerous for them.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: They can cause harm to themselves; they can also cause harm to motorists, who might have to suddenly swerve to avoid them and they might get into accidents.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: So, definitely, we are aligned in that we need to conduct more education and outreach efforts.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: On enforcement, I hear what the Member has said about increasing enforcement.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: So, while we are definitely considering it, we also have to be mindful that too much use of such technology may cause discomfort on the ground as well.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: Dr Yaacob Ibrahim, in his Budget Debate speech, also talked about whether or not there needs to be a community conversation around the use of technology in public spaces.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: We will bear in mind what the Member has mentioned and continuously look at better ways to conduct enforcement as well as education outreach efforts.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah
text: Pedestrians crossing the road and their eyes are glued to their mobile phones.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: So, that would be part and parcel of our education outreach efforts.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: It is not just about using your mobile phone when crossing the road.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: Even using your mobile phone while going up an escalator can be dangerous.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: When we reach out to pedestrians, especially when they are on the roads and, in this case, we are talking about elderly pedestrians, then all the more they need to be mindful of their surroundings.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: Having their eyes glued to the mobile phone is definitely a dangerous thing to do when they are crossing the road.
